What will happen as far as the bootloader setup goes? Does the Linux partition's boot manager take over just like on BIOS?
Planning to do a dual-boot between Windows 7 and Ubuntu Gnome on a UEFI machine

I believe grub takes over and then loads either linux or windows, but im not sure. I need to look into it myself. I've got 3 parts of my new desktop coming in the mail then i'm dual booting Windows 7 (pirated) and Mint.

I have dual booted on UEFI with GPT between Windows 10 and Debian.

Install Windows 7, fully update (very important), then install Ubuntu with Gnome.

Everything should work fine. The bootloader will come up just as it would with BIOS.

Note: A Windows update may eventually break your install. It has happened many times. Windows does something where it adds or modifies a partition (usually it's recovery partition or the efi partition) and that confuses the grub loader. It's kinda simple to fix though if it happens. You'll get a Grub Rescue prompt and you just need to tell it where the .efi file for grub is.

Then once you are in Ubuntu again, you need to do a update-grub in a terminal.

Another thing to keep in mind: Never boot the system without the OS drive installed. It will forget where the OS' are and next time you plug in the drive, it won't be able to boot from it.

The answer to fixing that is to use EasyUEFI and tell it where the OS' are again. It's a UEFI issue. There''s no way to change it AFAIK. This doesn't happen with all motherboards (as it is related to NVRAM used by the UEFI on the motherboard) because every company implements UEFI in it's own way. Both of my computers (ASUS & Gigabyte motherboards) do it though and it's quite annoying.

I use Easy2Boot to install my OS, as once it's setup, it's super fast and easy. Getting it to do UEFI though takes extra setup steps though.

Good luck and have fun.
